Evidence: Dual-tier update/setStatus write the PG leg via withTransaction→getDb() (ALS or env pool) and re-read via getById(id, undefined, workspaceId) (:511); no workspace handle is ever resolved from the row's workspace record. Socket/worker scopes have no ALS (RUN-007 class).
Reproduction: Dual-tier workspace whose record DB differs from env pool: call setStatus/update from socket scope - PG replica leg lands on the wrong pool or is outboxed; re-read may miss the just-written row.
Root cause: dualWrite/withTransaction use ambient getDb(); record-only tier contract says env URL is CLI-only, so the replica leg has no correct handle outside request ALS.
Impact: Split-DB deployments: PG replica diverges; update() can return null/stale after a successful local commit.
Proposed fix: Resolve a per-workspace handle (dbForWorkspace / tierContextFor→getWorkspaceDb) for the PG leg and re-read, or thread the caller handle end to end. Ship with a two-DB characterization test first.
Required tests: Integration: two DBs, socket-scope setStatus - replica row lands in the owning DB; update re-read returns the merged row.

Evidence: runtime_states cascade delete is wrapped in .catch(console.error) INSIDE the withTransaction callback; if the driver aborts the transaction on a failed statement, the swallowed rejection can roll back the agents delete itself, or leave the ledger row orphaned when it does not.
Reproduction: Force the runtime_states delete to fail (e.g. constraint/permission error) during delete(): observe agent row presence and ledger row afterwards.
Root cause: No FK between runtime_states.agent_id and agents.id (schema follow-up) + in-tx error swallowing.
Impact: Silent partial deletes / orphans; caller sees true/false unrelated to actual cascade state.
Proposed fix: Add the FK (migration, cascade) and let errors propagate; until then remove the in-tx .catch and log/queue after commit.
Required tests: Integration: failing cascade either rolls back wholly or leaves documented state; FK migration test.

Evidence: update() rewrites runtime_states.status to idle for every non-offline merged status, and agents.status follows the merged value; a profile edit of a working agent therefore marks it idle.
